title: Model intake: Regional GPU wedge & prefix-cache study
content:
Purpose:
Quick working worksheet to estimate short- and medium-term GPU slot and KV prefix-cache impact for a new medium-sized LLM (˜7B) being introduced across three regions. Focus is on the first 8 weeks after initial soft launch and on practical mitigations for cache fragmentation / eviction risk.

Assumptions (baseline):
- Model variant: 7.1B dense float16 (serving-optimized), sequence length typical 1024, KV per token footprint ~48 bytes (post-quant-kv optimizations).
- Typical request: 60 input tokens + 120 generated tokens (assume average 120 tokens produced).
- Average KV occupancy per active session = 180 tokens * 48B = 8.6 KB (rounded to 9 KB) in runtime.
- Warmup behavior: cold requests cause full KV population; steady-state requests mostly prefix hits if warm.
- Initial direct-traffic pattern: 60% NA (us-west/us-east split), 30% EU (eu-west), 10% APAC (asia-south).

Capacity parameters:
- Region GPU pool sizes (available for this model):
  - us-west: 120 slots (4xA100-equivalent)
  - us-east: 80 slots
  - eu-west: 64 slots
- KV memory reserved for model (soft limit): 28 GiB per region (configurable)
- Target SLO: p95 latency <= 220ms for generation-first-token, throughput target 90 RPS total steady-state across regions for tier-1 customers.

Scenarios evaluated:
1) Greenfield steady-state (no warmup pressure): 90 RPS evenly distributed by traffic share.
2) Soft-launch week 1 (bursty intake): new model exposed to 20% of traffic for 7 days with daily 30% peak spikes.
3) Full rollout week 4 (broader exposure): 60% of total traffic with occasional cross-region failover.
4) High-churn user mix (short sessions, high prefix diversity): increases KV fragmentation and raises eviction rate.

Numbers (estimates):
- Per-request KV bytes (runtime) = 9 KB.
- RPS -> concurrent sessions approximation: assume average response time per request 0.45s -> concurrency = RPS * 0.45.

Scenario 1: steady-state 90 RPS
- NA (60%) = 54 RPS -> concurrency 24.3 -> KV occupancy ~24.3 * 9KB ≈ 220 KB (negligible)
- EU (30%) = 27 RPS -> concurrency 12.2 -> KV ≈ 110 KB
- APAC (10%) = 9 RPS -> concurrency 4.1 -> KV ≈ 37 KB
- Conclusion: KV memory not a concern at steady low diversity. GPU slots used ~90 distributed; headroom present in us-west.

Scenario 2: soft-launch intake (20% of traffic directed to new model) with spikes
- Total RPS for model = 0.20 * baseline platform traffic estimate (assume baseline 1000 RPS) = 200 RPS -> concurrency 90 -> KV ~810 KB aggregate if sessions stay warm; but warmup causes transient hot allocations across many sessions.
- Regional split -> us-west 120 RPS (concurrency ~54) -> KV ~486 KB; us-east 40 RPS -> KV 162 KB; eu-west 40 RPS -> 162 KB; these are small absolute numbers but fragmentation matters: if prefixes are unique, per-GPU KV stripes may grow more because cold-working-sets span many models.
- GPU slot pressure: us-west 120 slots -> startup could saturate near capacity during spikes. Need admission control or staged rollout.

Scenario 3: full rollout (60% exposure)
- Model RPS = 0.60 * 1000 = 600 RPS -> concurrency 270 -> total KV ~2.4 MB. Regionally large pressure on slot usage and warmup overhead causing degraded p95 if not prewarmed.
- GPUs: us-west would require additional slot headroom beyond 120 to keep latency SLOs unless we route some load to eu-west or enable overflow to dedicated cold-tier.

High-churn variant impact:
- If user sessions are highly diverse (lots of unique prefixes), effective working set multiplies by factor 6–10 compared to steady prefixes. KV demand then could be measured in tens of MBs per region and eviction churn increases, causing p95 regressions and extra token compute for re-generation after eviction.

Risk matrix (high level):
- Eviction risk: low at steady-state, medium during soft-launch spikes, high under high-churn full rollout.
- Latency risk: increases with eviction + burst; secondary effect from GPU slot exhaustion causing queueing.
- Cost risk: warmup spike increases token compute and may double per-request cost during first 48 hours of exposure.

Mitigation playbook (operational recommendations):
1) Staged traffic ramp (canary -> gradual increase): start at 2% traffic for 48–72 hours, then 10%, 25%, 60%. Monitor KV hit rate and p95.
2) Prewarm seeding for heavy prefixes: use synthetic replay of top 200 known prefixes across regions to populate KV caches before broader exposure. Keep seeding job staggered to avoid simultaneous bursts.
3) Admission control knobs: implement per-region soft cap: throttle new-model requests when GPU utilization > 75% or KV eviction rate > 3%/min.
4) Overflow routing: have a fallback to a lower-latency smaller-quantized variant if slot pressure occurs. Configure automatic fallback with golden route to eu-west to relieve us-west.
5) Observe and adjust cache limits: if eviction is persistently high, increase KV reservation in region by 8–16 GiB as a short-term measure while adding GPU capacity.
6) Warmup backoff: if a seeding job causes upstream spikes, use randomized stagger and per-host sleep windows to smooth KV writes.

Monitoring dashboard checklist (key metrics):
- per-region GPU utilization (1m/5m/15m)
- per-region KV total bytes used (model-specific)
- KV eviction rate (evictions/min)
- KV hit rate (prefix hit%)
- p50/p95 generation latency and time-to-first-token
- admitted vs throttled request counts per region
- warmup job throughput and error rate

Immediate action items (owner names):
- Prewarm plan script + controlled replay (Priya) -> run in staging and small canary this week.
- Canary rollout gating thresholds + JIRA ticket (Carlos) -> INFRA-1329 to track gating rules.
- Dashboard panels (Ava) -> add KV eviction and hit-rate charts for this model.

Open questions / unknowns to resolve before week-4 rollout:
- Confirm per-token KV bytes after latest quant-kv patch (kernel team) — could reduce footprint by ~15% which materially lowers risk.
- Validate traffic baseline assumption (platform analytics) — 1000 RPS assumed. If baseline is 2x, all numbers scale and risk increases.
- Decide overflow routing priority order for region failover.

Notes and quick references:
- Related experiments: small prewarm job in qa reduced cold p95 by ~42% in internal test (see linked PR).
- Cost estimate: one additional A100-equivalent fleet shard adds ~40 slots; incremental monthly cost ~ $45k (depends on cloud provider).

Appendix (quick table of mitigation timing):
- Week -1: smoke tests + prewarm script dry run (Priya)
- Week 0: 2% canary (24–72h), monitor KV eviction
- Week 1: 10% ramp if stable
- Week 2: 25% ramp + increase KV reservation if eviction > 1%/min
- Week 4: 60% exposure rolling if p95 SLO + eviction within thresholds

Working notes (scratch):
- If early telemetry shows >10% eviction we should pause rollout and spin additional capacity.
- Consider temporary client-side caching to reduce server KV churn for some use cases.
summary: Working capacity worksheet for a new 7B model rollout across three regions focusing on GPU slot pressure and KV prefix-cache fragmentation; includes scenario estimates, mitigation playbook, monitoring checklist, and action items.
